(bucrilate) Profile A number of cyanoacrylate compounds have been used as surgi- cal tissue adhesives. They include: • bucrilate (bucrylate; isobutyl 2-cyanoacrylate, C8H11NO2 = 153.2) • enbucrilate (butyl 2-cyanoacrylate, C8H11NO2 = 153.2), • mecrilate (mecrylate; methyl 2-cyanoacrylate, C5H5NO2 = 111.1) • ocrilate (ocrylate; octil 2-cyanoacrylate, C12H19NO2 = 209.3). Some cyanoacrylates are used for household purposes and as nail fixatives and others have been investigated as tubal occlusive agents for female sterilisation, for sclerotherapy in bleeding gas- tric varices (see under Monoethanolamine, p.2346), and for em- bolisation of intracranial vascular lesions.
